
```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
library(vmTools)
library(data.table)

print_tree <- function(x, level = Inf) vmTools:::dir_tree(x, level = level)
```

The Symlink Tool comes with four symlink types: `best`, `latest`, `keep` and
`remove`. You can add your own, for example `stalled` for runs waiting on an
input. A type you add is recorded in the root folder itself, so every user of
that root sees it.

| Built-in type | `is_singleton` | Symlink name in the root |
|---|---|---|
| `best` | `TRUE` | `best` |
| `latest` | `TRUE` | `latest` |
| `keep` | `FALSE` | `keep_<version_name>` |
| `remove` | `FALSE` | `remove_<version_name>` |

# Add a symlink type

Build a tool on your root as usual, then add the type with one call:

```{r setup_root, include = FALSE, eval = flag_eval}
demo_base  <- file.path(tempdir(), "slt_types_demo")
model_root <- file.path(demo_base, "model_root")
dir.create(model_root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
model_root <- clean_path(model_root)
.opt_mc    <- options(mc.cores = 1L)
```

```{r add_type, eval = flag_eval}
slt <- SLT$new(root_list = list("model_root" = model_root))

slt$update_symlink_registry(
  symlink_type   = "stalled"
  , is_singleton = FALSE
  , operation    = "add"
)

names(slt$get_symlink_registry())
```

That is the only step. The type is recorded in the root, so it is there in
every later R session and for every other user of the root.

## The arguments

| Argument | What to pass |
|---|---|
| `symlink_type` | The name of your type, in lowercase. It cannot be a built-in name. |
| `is_singleton` | `TRUE` or `FALSE`. See the next table. |
| `operation` | `"add"` for a type the root does not have yet. `"update"` and `"drop"` are covered under Editing the registry. |

Without a tool, `update_symlink_disk_registry()` does the same for any root
folder. It takes the same arguments, plus `root` and `verbose`.

## Choosing `is_singleton`

`is_singleton` is the one decision a symlink type needs: can one version hold
the mark, or many?

| `is_singleton` | Symlink name in the root | Versions that can hold it | Built-in examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRUE` | `<type>` | one per root; marking another version moves it | `best`, `latest` |
| `FALSE` | `<type>_<version_name>` | as many as you mark | `keep`, `remove` |

Once a type is added, its name is reserved in that way: a version folder
cannot be called `stalled_anything`.

## Use the type

Mark with it like any built-in type.

```{r use_type, eval = flag_eval}
slt$make_new_version_folder("2025_01_01.01")
slt$make_new_version_folder("2025_01_01.02")

slt$mark("stalled", "2025_01_01.01", user_entry = list(comment = "waiting on inputs"))
slt$mark("stalled", "2025_01_01.02", user_entry = list(comment = "waiting on inputs"))

slt$roundup("stalled", return_as = "version_name")
```

```{r use_type_tree, eval = flag_eval}
print_tree(model_root, level = 1)
```

---

# How a tool uses the registry file

A tool does not keep its own list of symlink types. Each time it is used it
reads the registry file of every root, so a type a teammate adds to a root is
there at your tool's next call.

```
SLT$new(), roundups,                        mark(), unmark(),
get_symlink_registry()                      delete_version_folders()
          |                                           |
          +---------------------+---------------------+
                                |
                                v
            read .symlink_registry.csv in every root
                                |
                                v
   do two roots give one symlink type a different is_singleton?
                                |
                                +-- yes --> STOP, nothing changed
                                |           the error lists each root's
                                |           is_singleton and the call to run
                                no
                                |
                                v
    the tool's symlink types = built-in types + types on the files
          |                                           |
          v                                           v
  nothing is written                    first, the files are repaired:
                                        a root with no file gets one, and
                                        a type one root has and another
                                        lacks is copied over
                                                      |
                                                      v
                                          then the operation runs
```

Building a tool and rounding up never write to a root, so both work on a
root you can only read.

## Several roots

The roots of one tool must agree on each type's `is_singleton`. If they do
not, the tool stops and prints the call that fixes it:

```{r roots_disagree, eval = flag_eval, error = TRUE}
other_root <- file.path(demo_base, "other_root")
dir.create(other_root)

update_symlink_disk_registry(
  other_root, "stalled", is_singleton = TRUE, operation = "add", verbose = FALSE
)

SLT$new(root_list = list("model_root" = model_root, "other_root" = other_root))
```

A root that simply lacks a type is not a disagreement. It gets the type from
its sibling roots the next time the tool marks, unmarks or deletes.

---

# Editing the registry

This section is for changing a type later, or for reading an error.
`slt$update_symlink_registry()` edits every root of a tool;
`update_symlink_disk_registry()` edits the roots you name. Both follow the
same rules.

## The registry file

Each root carries one small file, `.symlink_registry.csv`, with one row per
symlink type. The built-in types are listed first. The tool writes this file;
it is not meant to be edited by hand, and a hand-edited file is refused when
it is read.

```{r show_file, eval = flag_eval}
read.csv(file.path(model_root, ".symlink_registry.csv"))
```

## Change `is_singleton`, or drop a type

The same function does both, with a different `operation`:

```{r change_calls, eval = FALSE}
# a type on file, with a different is_singleton
slt$update_symlink_registry("stalled", is_singleton = TRUE, operation = "update")

# remove a type from the file
slt$update_symlink_registry("stalled", operation = "drop")
```

What happens depends on the `operation` argument and on the symlink type's row
in the root's file:

- `absent`: the file has no row for the symlink type
- `matches`: a row exists and its `is_singleton` equals the argument
- `differs`: a row exists and its `is_singleton` is the other value

```{r outcomes, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(vmTools:::get_disk_registry_outcomes())
```

`write` changes the file, `skip` leaves it, and `stop` refuses the whole call
before any root's file is written.

## When a change is refused

An `update` or a `drop` is refused while symlinks of that type exist. After
the change they would belong to no symlink type the tool knows.

```
update_symlink_disk_registry(root, symlink_type, is_singleton, operation)
      |
      v
in each root's file, the symlink type's row is
absent, matches is_singleton, or differs
      |
      v
is the operation refused in any root?
   add     where the row differs
   update  where the row is absent
      |
      +-- yes --> STOP, nothing written
      |           the error names the root and the operation to use
      no
      |
      v
update or drop: do links of the symlink type exist?
      |
      +-- yes --> STOP, nothing written
      |           the error prints the unmark() calls to run first
      no
      |
      v
write each root's file
(roots already as asked are left alone)
```

The two `stalled` symlinks made above block a change, and the error prints the
calls that clear the way:

```{r refused, eval = flag_eval, error = TRUE}
slt$update_symlink_registry("stalled", is_singleton = TRUE, operation = "update")
```

## Messages and what to do

| The message says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `already on file with this is_singleton; nothing changed` | The root already has what you asked for. | Nothing. |
| `already on file with a different is_singleton; use operation = 'update'` | You used `"add"` for a type the root has, with a different `is_singleton`. | Repeat the call with `operation = "update"`. |
| `not on file; use operation = 'add'` | You used `"update"` for a type the root does not have. | Repeat the call with `operation = "add"`. |
| `live and ... dangling link(s) of this type exist` | Symlinks of the type are in the way. | Run the `unmark()` lines printed in the error, then repeat the call. |
| `Root folders disagree on is_singleton for a symlink (shortcut) type` | Two roots record the same type differently. | Run the printed `update_symlink_disk_registry()` call on the root you want to change. |
| `Built-in symlink (shortcut) types are fixed by the package` | You passed `best`, `latest`, `keep` or `remove`. | Choose another name. |
| `symlink_type must be lowercase` | The name has a capital letter. Windows and macOS compare names ignoring case. | Use the lowercase spelling the message suggests. |

See also `?update_symlink_disk_registry`.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
if (flag_eval) {
  unlink(demo_base, recursive = TRUE)
  options(.opt_mc)
}
options(.opt_width)
```
